chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the water with which the deceased is washed, asking: 'What is its limit?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'The limit of washing the deceased is that he is washed until he becomes clean, if Allah wills.'

He said: And he wrote to him: 'Is it permissible that the deceased is washed and the water poured upon him enters into a cesspool well, or that a man performs the ablution for prayer and the water of his ablution is poured into a cesspool?' So he (peace be upon him) signed: 'That will end up in the cesspools.'
ai.seo_question: What is the limit of water used to wash the deceased and can it be used for ablution?
ai.summary: In this correspondence from Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (AS) to his secretary, the legal limit for washing water is defined by the removal of impurity rather than a fixed volume, emphasizing the principle of *tahur* (purification). The text further clarifies the ritual purity of wastewater by permitting the disposal of both bathing water and ablution water into a cesspool (*kaniif*), reflecting the practical juristic concerns of the late Imams period regarding domestic hygiene and ritual validity.
